properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 17 at 4:19PM EDT until October 17 at 5:15PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
FFWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northern Broward County in southeastern Florida...
Southern Palm Beach County in southeastern Florida...

* Until 515 PM EDT.

* At 419 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
3 and 4 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of
1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Coral Springs, Deerfield Beach, Margate, Coconut Creek, Parkland,
Godfrey Road, Mission Bay, Boca Pointe, Hamptons At Boca Raton,
Boca Del Mar, Hillsboro Pines, Hillsboro Ranches, Sandalfoot Cove,
Ramblewood East and South County Regional Park.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 17 at 3:46PM EDT until October 17 at 4:45PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
SMWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 0-20 nm...

* Until 445 PM EDT.

* At 346 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located near Jupiter Inlet Colony, moving north at
5 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can can quickly form and capsize boats,
damage vessels and create locally hazardous seas. Make
sure all on board are wearing life jackets. Expect wind
gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher waves,
lightning and heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are
wearing life jackets. Return to safe harbor if possible.

* Locations impacted include...
Jupiter Inlet Colony, Jupiter Inlet, Jupiter Island, Hobe Sound
Beach, and Tequesta.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor immediately as gusty winds and high waves are
expected.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 17 at 3:46PM EDT until October 20 at 5:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents,
large breaking waves expected, and strong longshore currents in
the surf zone. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves
of 8 to 14 feet expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal
Flood Warning, 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level
expected in low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 5 PM EDT Tuesday. For
the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT this evening. For
the Coastal Flood Warning, until 5 PM EDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
expected in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of vehicles
will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be inundated,
especially around high tide. There is a possibility of being
stranded on Hatteras Island for multiple days. This could be
life threatening if you have an emergency. Dangerous swimming
and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This has the potential to be a long
duration event bringing more significant ocean overwash impacts
to vulnerable oceanside areas through multiple high tide cycles
into next week. Minor soundside water level rises will also be
possible.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of unknown
depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property. Prepare for being stranded on Hatteras Island for
multiple days. Prepare for disruptions to ferries by this evening
and lasting into at least part of next week.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Beaver Creek near Electra affecting Wilbarger and Wichita Counties.

For the Beaver Creek (NW TX)...including Electra...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Beaver Creek near Electra.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening to Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 26.0 feet, Flood levels up to 2 feet in depth cover
farm and range lands... and may inundate some oil and gas
facilities... along and near the creek in southern Wilbarger County
and southwestern Wichita County.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:00 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 17.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 24.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
tomorrow evening to a crest of 25.6 feet early Monday afternoon.
It will then fall below flood stage early Tuesday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 24.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 25.7
feet on 10/14/2018.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 215 AM CDT.

...TYPHOON CHAMPI NOW A DANGEROUS CATEGORY 4 MOVING WEST INTO GUAM
COASTAL WATERS...

.NEW INFORMATION...
None.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended actions for
people on Guam and on Rota, Tinian and Saipan in the Northern
Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
A Typhoon Warning continues for Guam and Rota.

A Tropical Storm Warning and a Typhoon Watch continues for Tinian
and Saipan.

A Flood Watch is in effect for Rota, Tinian and Saipan in the
Northern Marianas. Please listen closely for any Flood Warnings that
might be in effect for your area.

A Flash Flood Warning is now in effect for Guam.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 4 AM ChST...the center of Typhoon Champi (29W) was located near
latitude 13.1N...longitude 144.9E. This was about 25 miles southeast
of Guam. Storm motion was west, 280 degrees, at 15 mph. Storm
intensity was 140 mph. This general forecast track will take Champi
about 15 miles south of Guam as a Category 4 typhoon as it intensifies
further the next few days west of the Marianas.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Typhoon Champi (29W) has been undergoing rapid intensification
today. As a result it is now a dangerous category 4 typhoon. It is
expected to pass a little south of Guam as a super typhoon within
the next 12 hours. This may potentially bring devastating wind
conditions to much of Guam during passage.

.PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...
properties.instruction:
Take small loose objects indoors. Identify suitable shelter. Stock
up a few days worth of food and water. If no concrete shelter is
available look for a cave or something similar. Take action to
protect food crops or other possessions as appropriate.

change. However, guidance supports a passage through Guam coastal

through the region as a category 4 super typhoon Sunday morning.

high as 25 feet during closest passage of Champi. Dangerous sea
conditions may continue into Monday.

are expected to be extremely dangerous for small craft, and dangerous
for any vessels of larger size. As Typhoon Champi approaches the
